question: How the original feeds gfx/FX/hierarchy.fx: the vertices, every parameter, the render states and the order the hierarchy lines are drawn in.

structs.name: HierarchyLines
structs.comment: The object the in-game screen keeps at CInGameIdler +0x1DE0 for the selected unit's hierarchy lines: made as the screen is built (VA 0x6492EF, 0x40 bytes, every word zero, the phase 0.0), destroyed by HierarchyLines_Destruct in the screen's teardown. No vftable. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, sections 2 and 7.
structs.evidence: The constructor's stores at VA 0x6492FE..0x64932B (+0, +4, +8, +0x10, byte +0x14, float +0x18, +0x1C..+0x2C, byte +0x30, +0x34..+0x3C) end at +0x3C, and `push 0x40` before operator new at 0x6492E8. The mesh at +0x1C is a MeshBuffer (0x24 bytes in the record), so +0x1C + 0x24 = 0x40 fills it exactly. What would show it wrong: a store or read past +0x3F through the object's pointer.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_LoadShader
addresses.comment: **Loads what the hierarchy lines are drawn with.** Two callers: LoadEverything (VA 0x6319D9) and VA 0x43BBBE. Keeps the graphics in g_HierarchyGraphics. CreateVertexDeclaration (device slot 86) of HierarchyVertexDecl_Elements - FLOAT2 POSITION0 at 0, FLOAT3 TEXCOORD0 at 8, D3DCOLOR COLOR0 at 20, stride 24 - into g_HierarchyVertexDecl; on failure MessageBoxA 'CreateVertexDeclaration failed!! (HierarchyVertexDecl)' and FatalExit(1). The effect `/FX/hierarchy.fx`, its path made from the game's directory settings (the global at VA 0x1A85558, +0xB8 / +0x25C by its mode +0x4C) as the other map effects' are: FxHandler_Reload under the key `Hierarchy` first, then FxHandler_Register(the graphics' effect handler +0x6BCFC, path, `Hierarchy`, device), and g_HierarchyEffect = the handler's list entry for the index it answers (null for 0). Then by name: the handles of WorldViewProjectionMatrix, CameraPosition, LineTexture and Time (effect slot 9) and the technique `Hierarchy` (slot 13). Last the texture `/mapitems/hierarchy_line.tga`, any index already held released first (VA 0xA610E0), registered with the graphics' texture handler (+0x158, VA 0xA60F30) into g_HierarchyTextureIndex - TextureHandler_LoadFile opens it as hierarchy_line.dds where that exists, which is the only copy the install has. `ret 4`. EBX is saved and zeroed before any read, so it is not an argument (the former no_signature said otherwise). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Read VA 0x883290..0x88375E end to end: `mov eax,[ebp+8]; mov [0x1a8cb5c],eax`, `call [ecx+0x158]` with (device, 0x170ABD8, 0x1A8CB40), the strings at 0x883391/0x8833FC/0x883471/0x883522/0x883544/0x88355C/0x883574/0x88358C/0x8835B9, `call 0xa624f0` then `call 0xa61dd0`, the stores to 0x1A8CB44..0x1A8CB60, `ret 4` at 0x88375E. EBX: `push ebx` at 0x8832B1 is the callee save, `xor ebx,ebx` at 0x8832D1 precedes its first use. Callers by findRefs --callers: 0x43BBBE, 0x6319D9. What would show it wrong: a read of EBX before 0x8832D1, or a second ret.
addresses.revises: Signature added (was no_signature claiming EBX is read before written, which the listing refutes); comment now gives the declaration, the reload-then-register order, the globals and the texture's .dds.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_Draw
addresses.signature: void __stdcall HierarchyLines_Draw(MapCamera* camera, MeshBuffer* mesh, float phase)
addresses.comment: **Draws the hierarchy mesh through hierarchy.fx.** Nothing where the mesh has no primitives (+0x10) or the graphics have no current view (CGraphics +0x6BC88). Device first: ZWRITEENABLE 0, ZENABLE 0 (SetRenderState, not put back afterwards). Then on g_HierarchyEffect: SetTechnique(Hierarchy); Begin(&passes, 0); **WorldViewProjectionMatrix = D3DXMatrixMultiply(view slot 91 (+0x16C), view slot 93 (+0x174))** of the current view's camera (+0x1C) - the scene's view x projection, no world matrix (SetMatrix); **CameraPosition = (camera x_settled +0x33C, y_settled +0x340)**, SetFloatArray of 2; LineTexture = the texture handler's entry g_HierarchyTextureIndex (graphics + index * 0x2C + 0x15C), null where the index is -1 or above 9999; **Time = phase** (SetFloat, where the handle exists). For each pass: BeginPass, CommitChanges, VertexBuffer_Draw(mesh) - an indexed triangle list of the mesh's vertices -; then CameraPosition.x = (float)((double)x - (double)(float)map width, CMap +0x2A74), CommitChanges, the mesh again; EndPass. End. So the mesh is drawn where it is and **once more a map width to the east, never to the west**. `ret 0xC`. One caller, CInGameIdler_Render (VA 0x657152). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Read VA 0x883030..0x88328C: `cmp [eax+0x10],0` on arg 2; `[0x1a8cb5c]+0x6bc88`; device slot 57 (0xE4) with (0xE,0) and (7,0); effect slots 58 (0xE8), 63 (0xFC, flags 0), 32 (0x80, count 2, from arg1+0x33C/+0x340), 38 (0x98), 52 (0xD0), 30 (0x78); D3DXMatrixMultiply (import 0xD2B438) with M1 = slot 0x16C, M2 = slot 0x174; the loop 0x8831C3..0x883270 with slots 64/65/66 and two calls of 0xAD4C30; `subsd` of the converted [0x1a8557c]+0x2A74 at 0x883224; End (slot 67) and `ret 0xc`. Slot numbering is d3dx9_42's ID3DXEffect as FINDINGS-mapdraw.md lists it. What would show it wrong: a different import at 0xD2B438 (pefile names it D3DXMatrixMultiply), or a third draw call.
addresses.revises: Signature typed (MapCamera*, MeshBuffer*); comment now gives the Z states, the exact matrix, the CameraPosition source and its second value, the texture lookup and that the second copy is one map width east only, replacing 'by all appearance the two copies either side of its seam'.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_AddLine
addresses.signature: void __fastcall HierarchyLines_AddLine(void* context@ESI, CUnit* unit@EDX, int* from@stack:4, int* to@stack:8, bool outOfReach@stack:12)
addresses.comment: **One line of the hierarchy: four 24-byte vertices and six 16-bit indices**, written at the context's cursors (context +0 the locked vertices, +4 the locked indices, +8 vertices so far, +0xC indices so far, +0x10 the selected unit). Colour (ARGB) and range: out of radio range 0xFF800000 and 0.0; otherwise 1.0 and 0xFF007800 for the selected unit itself, 0xFF1432C8 where its commander (+0x1E0) is the selected unit, 0xFF6464D2 where its commander's commander is, 0xFFC8C8C8 further down. Half width w = (float)((double)(size + 1) * 0.2), size from the **unit's own** oob_level by the jump table at rva 0x483010: 0 theatre 5, 1 army group 4, 2 army 3, 3 corps 2, 4 division 1 where it has more than one brigade (+0x40 > 1) else 0, 5 navy 1, 6 air 0, anything else 0. f = from (the unit's province's unit point), t = to (the commander's), as floats. **The seam**: where t.x - f.x > W/2, t.x -= W; else where f.x - t.x > W/2, f.x -= W (W the map width CMap +0x2A74, W/2 cached once in g_HierarchyHalfMapWidth) - the eastern end is moved a map width west. d = t - f, L = sqrtf(d.x^2 + d.y^2), a = d * (w / L). Vertices in order, each (x, y, u, v, range, colour): (f.x - a.y, f.y + a.x, 0, 0), (f.x + a.y, f.y - a.x, 1, 0), (t.x - a.y, t.y + a.x, 0, V), (t.x + a.y, t.y - a.x, 1, V), with **V = L / (2w) * 0.2**; indices n, n+1, n+2, n+1, n+3, n+2 for the vertex count n before the line. `ret 0xC`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, sections 4 and 7.
addresses.evidence: Read VA 0x882B30..0x88300A: the colour ladder 0x882B36..0x882B8A; the table at 0x883010 = {0x882BA6 (5), 0x882BAD (4), 0x882BB4 (3), 0x882BBB (2), 0x882BC2 (+0x40 > 1), 0x882BCC (1), 0x882BD0 (0)}; `inc eax; cvtsi2ss; mulsd [0x160A260]` (0.2); the seam at 0x882C26..0x882CDB with [0x160A308] = 0.5 and [0x160A360] = 2.0; `call 0x402000` (fld; CRT sqrt; fstp float); the x87 `fadd st0,st0; fdivp` then `fmul [0x160A260]` for V; the six word stores and the 24 dword/float stores per vertex at +0..+0x14. What would show it wrong: a vertex store order other than the one listed, which the offsets +0..+0x14 after each `add [esi+8],1` fix.
addresses.revises: Comment: the seam moves whichever end is further east a map width west (it said the far end's x is moved), the size of each oob_level including the lone-brigade division, navy and air, the exact vertex order and the index pattern.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_AddUnit
addresses.comment: Adds a unit's line where it is a land unit (slot 15) aboard neither a fleet nor an air unit (its slot 9 object's +0x300 and +0x304 both 0), has a commander (+0x1E0), and the commander's province (+0x130) is not its own: HierarchyLines_AddLine(from = the unit's province's unit point, template +0x64/+0x68; to = the commander's; CUnit::IsOutOfRadioRange of the unit). **The commander's own aboard test is never made**: where the commander is a land unit the code asks slot 9 of the *unit* again, which has already answered - so a commander that is aboard something still gets the line, to whatever province it is in. Always answers true. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, sections 3 and 7.
addresses.evidence: VA 0x882AC8..0x882AEA: after `call [edx+0x3c]` on edi (the commander), both slot 9 calls are `mov eax,[esi]; ... mov ecx,esi` - the unit in ESI, not the commander in EDI. The counter HierarchyLines_CountUnit (VA 0x8829F0) has no commander test at all, so the two agree on the number of lines. What would show it wrong: an `mov ecx,edi` before either slot 9 call.
addresses.revises: Comment: the commander's aboard test does not exist (the code re-tests the unit); from is the unit's point and to the commander's, stated explicitly.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_Rebuild
addresses.comment: **Makes the mesh of the hierarchy lines for a selected unit.** With no unit, clears +0x14 and returns. Otherwise empties the records, remembers the unit's commander at +0x10, and counts: HierarchyLines_CountUnit on the unit and HierarchyLines_CountBelow on each unit under it, which also records each land unit aboard nothing with its province. The mesh (+0x1C) has its vertex and index buffers released (the declaration pointer is zeroed first, so the shared declaration is not), its counts and FVF zeroed, and with no line +0x14 is cleared. Otherwise the mesh is made in the managed pool (+0x30 = 1) with g_HierarchyVertexDecl: VertexBuffer_Create(4 x lines, stride 0x18, FVF 0, not dynamic), IndexBuffer_Create(6 x lines) - a triangle list, the kind +0x3C being 0 from construction; both locked whole (flags 0), and HierarchyLines_AddBelow walks the unit and everything under it with the context {vertices, indices, 0, 0, the unit, W * 0.5}; both unlocked, +0x14 = 1. The phase +0x18 is not touched. The object is CInGameIdler +0x1DE0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, sections 3 and 7.
addresses.evidence: Read VA 0x883890..0x883A60: the early `mov byte [eax+0x14],0; ret 8`; the erase loop; `mov [ebx+0x10],ecx`; calls 0x8829F0 and 0x883AB0; `mov dword [ebx+0x24],0` before the three Release calls; `mov byte [ecx+0x30],1`; `push 0; push 0; push 0x18; push count*4` into 0xAD4510 and `count*6` into 0xAD48B0; the two Lock calls (slot 11, 0x2C) with flags 0 for a non-dynamic buffer; the context built at [ebp-0x24]..[ebp-0x10]; the two Unlock calls (slot 12, 0x30); `mov byte [eax+0x14],1; ret 8`. Construction zeroes +0x3C (VA 0x64932B). What would show it wrong: a write of the mesh's primitive kind (+0x3C) anywhere in the object's life.
addresses.revises: Signature's first parameter typed HierarchyLines*; comment adds the pool, FVF, lock flags, the declaration, the context's layout and that the phase is left alone.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_CountUnit
addresses.comment: HierarchyLines_Rebuild's count of one unit: where the unit is a land unit (slot 15) aboard nothing (slot 9 object's +0x300 and +0x304), adds one to the context's +4 when it has a commander (+0x1E0) in another province (+0x130), and in either case appends {unit, its province} to the records vector the context's +0 points at - the lines object's +0, which HierarchyLines_IsCurrent compares later. Always answers true. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Read VA 0x8829F0..0x882A61: the slot 15 and two slot 9 tests on ESI, `inc dword [edi+4]` under the commander and province test, then `mov edi,[edi]` and the call of 0x883B30 with {esi, [esi+0x130]}; `mov al,1`, bare `ret`. Two callers, 0x8838EF (Rebuild) and 0x883ABD (CountBelow). What would show it wrong: a stack argument read through ebp+8.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_CountBelow
addresses.comment: HierarchyLines_CountUnit on a unit, then itself on each unit under it (CUnit +0x1E4), in that list's order. The counting twin of HierarchyLines_AddBelow. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Read VA 0x883AB0..0x883AEA: the call of 0x8829F0 with EAX = the context and ESI = the unit, the loop over [unit+0x1E4] calling 0x883AB0 with `add esp,8`, bare `ret`. What would show it wrong: a second caller passing something else in the first slot.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_Destruct
addresses.comment: Takes a HierarchyLines apart: the mesh's declaration pointer (+0x24) zeroed, then its vertex and index buffers (+0x1C, +0x20) Released and its counts and FVF zeroed, and the records vector (+0) freed. One caller, the in-game screen's teardown (VA 0x649829), which deletes the object after it. `ret 4`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Read VA 0x883770..0x8837FA: `mov [esi+0x24],edi` (0) before the Release calls on +0x1C/+0x20/+0x24, the zeroing of +0x1C..+0x38, the free of [esi], `ret 4`. findRefs --callers: 0x649829, followed by `call 0xb95f9b` (operator delete) on the same pointer. What would show it wrong: another caller that keeps using the object.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_Render
addresses.comment: **The in-game screen draws a frame.** Called once, at the end of CInGameIdler::Update (VA 0x656756); in no virtual table. 0x256E10 to the `ret 4` at rva 0x258EBD (the bare `ret` at rva 0x258978 is a catch funclet's). Makes its own clock at +0x1934 on first use (g_random_object slot 1, started); **g_RenderIdleSeconds = that clock now less g_RenderEndTime**, the seconds since the last frame's Present. In order, as far as read: BeginScene, Clear(0, NULL, TARGET|ZBUFFER|STENCIL, 0xFF808080, 1.0, 0), MapGraphics_DrawScene, VA 0x8482F0 on +0x1DDC (another effect's meshes, not read; it sets ZWRITEENABLE 0 and ZENABLE 0 and no blend state), then **the hierarchy lines** (VA 0x657061..0x657152) where all hold: hierarchy_lines (+0x1DE0) exists, render_hierarchy (settings +0xE8) is set, alwaysCounters (settings +0xF9) is set or the map camera's height (+0x1C80, MapCamera +0x348) is strictly above counter_distance (settings +0xFC), the height is strictly under 500.0, and the lines' +0x14 is set; then **phase (+0x18) += g_RenderIdleSeconds where that is above 0.2, else the float 0.2**, less 100 once strictly above 100, and HierarchyLines_Draw(map camera +0x1938, lines +0x1C, phase); then the unit layers (VA 0x641950), FILLMODE SOLID, further draws not read, EndScene, Present (VA 0xA73B80), and g_RenderEndTime = the clock. Under the layer-mask bit settings +0xEC & 0x2000000 it shows four of its timings x 10000. The name is ours, after CFrontEnd_Render. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, section 7.
addresses.evidence: Extent: the only run of two or more int3 between VA 0x656E00 and 0x659000 is the 12 before 0x656E10; the one `ret 4` is at 0x658EBD after the SEH restore, and the bare `ret` at 0x658978 is `mov eax,0x658979; ret`, a catch funclet's continuation. One caller (findRefs --callers: 0x656756), `vtable.py --holding` none. The gate and phase at 0x657061..0x657152 read whole; the constants 0.2 (VA 0x160A260 double, 0x171618C float), 100.0 (0x160A358), 500.0 (0x160A538); the writes of 0x1BEA47C at 0x656EA1 and 0x1BEA484 at 0x658EA7, after `call 0xa73b80` whose body is device slot 17, Present. Name `inferred`: the role is what the body does; the record has no name for it. What would show it wrong: a second caller from a different screen.

addresses.name: HierarchyLines_AddLine_SizeCases
addresses.comment: Seven entries, HierarchyLines_AddLine's switch on the unit's oob_level 0..6: the counter size 5, 4, 3, 2, (more than one brigade ? 1 : 0), 1, 0. Anything above 6 is 0.
addresses.evidence: The seven dwords at VA 0x883010: 0x882BA6, 0x882BAD, 0x882BB4, 0x882BBB, 0x882BC2, 0x882BCC, 0x882BD0, each a `mov eax, N` or the `+0x40 > 1` test; `jmp [eax*4 + 0x883010]` at 0x882B9F after `cmp eax, 6; ja`. What would show it wrong: nothing short of a different image.

addresses.name: HierarchyVertexDecl_Elements
addresses.comment: The hierarchy lines' D3DVERTEXELEMENT9 list, static in .data: {stream 0, offset 0, FLOAT2, DEFAULT, POSITION 0}, {0, 8, FLOAT3, DEFAULT, TEXCOORD 0}, {0, 20, D3DCOLOR, DEFAULT, COLOR 0}, D3DDECL_END - hierarchy.fx's VS_INPUT, a 24-byte vertex. Its one reference is HierarchyLines_LoadShader's CreateVertexDeclaration.
addresses.evidence: The 32 bytes at VA 0x170ABD8 decoded as D3DVERTEXELEMENT9 (WORD, WORD, BYTE x4): types 1, 2, 4, usages 0, 5, 10, then stream 0xFF type 17. findRefs --address: one reference, VA 0x8832C9 (`push 0x170abd8`). What would show it wrong: a writer in .text, which the same search would have listed.

addresses.name: g_HierarchyVertexDecl
addresses.comment: IDirect3DVertexDeclaration9* made from HierarchyVertexDecl_Elements by HierarchyLines_LoadShader; HierarchyLines_Rebuild puts it on the mesh (+8), where VertexBuffer_Draw sets it.
addresses.evidence: The out pointer of CreateVertexDeclaration at VA 0x8832C4, read at 0x883998 into [edi+8] of the mesh. What would show it wrong: another writer.

addresses.name: g_HierarchyEffect
addresses.comment: The ID3DXEffect of gfx/FX/hierarchy.fx, from the effect handler's list (HierarchyLines_LoadShader); HierarchyLines_Draw uses it.
addresses.evidence: Written at VA 0x883527 from the handler list entry FxHandler_Register's index names; every ID3DXEffect call in 0x883030..0x88328C goes through it. What would show it wrong: a writer outside LoadShader.

addresses.name: g_HierarchyHandle_WorldViewProjectionMatrix
addresses.comment: D3DXHANDLE of hierarchy.fx's WorldViewProjectionMatrix (HierarchyLines_LoadShader); HierarchyLines_Draw sets view x projection through it.
addresses.evidence: Stored at VA 0x883535 from GetParameterByName(NULL, 'WorldViewProjectionMatrix'); read at 0x883148 for SetMatrix.

addresses.name: g_HierarchyHandle_CameraPosition
addresses.comment: D3DXHANDLE of hierarchy.fx's CameraPosition (float2); HierarchyLines_Draw sets it twice a pass.
addresses.evidence: Stored at VA 0x88354D; read at 0x883125 and 0x88321A for SetFloatArray(..., 2).

addresses.name: g_HierarchyHandle_Technique
addresses.comment: D3DXHANDLE of hierarchy.fx's technique `Hierarchy` (GetTechniqueByName); HierarchyLines_Draw's SetTechnique.
addresses.evidence: Stored at VA 0x883599 from effect slot 13 with 'Hierarchy'; read at 0x88308A for slot 58.

addresses.name: g_HierarchyHandle_LineTexture
addresses.comment: D3DXHANDLE of hierarchy.fx's LineTexture; HierarchyLines_Draw's SetTexture.
addresses.evidence: Stored at VA 0x883565; read at 0x883186 for slot 52.

addresses.name: g_HierarchyHandle_Time
addresses.comment: D3DXHANDLE of hierarchy.fx's Time; HierarchyLines_Draw sets the phase through it where it is not null.
addresses.evidence: Stored at VA 0x88357D; read at 0x883195 and tested before SetFloat (slot 30).

addresses.name: g_HierarchyGraphics
addresses.comment: The CGraphics HierarchyLines_LoadShader was given: its device (+0x64), current view (+0x6BC88) and texture handler entries (+0x15C, 0x2C each) are what HierarchyLines_Draw and HierarchyLines_Rebuild use.
addresses.evidence: Written at VA 0x8832B4 from LoadShader's argument; read at 0x883049, 0x88306E, 0x883169, 0x8831E4, 0x88324D and 0x88397B.

addresses.name: g_HierarchyTextureIndex
addresses.comment: The texture handler's index of hierarchy_line.tga (opened as .dds); HierarchyLines_Draw takes the texture from the graphics' entry index * 0x2C + 0x15C where the index is neither -1 nor above 9999. Released before a reload where above 0.
addresses.evidence: Written at VA 0x8836D5 from VA 0xA60F30's answer; `cmp ecx,ebx; jle` before the release at 0x8836A5; the range test and `imul eax,eax,0x2c` at 0x883158..0x883172.

addresses.name: g_RenderIdleSeconds
addresses.comment: Float seconds: at the head of CInGameIdler_Render, the idler's frame clock (+0x1934) less g_RenderEndTime - the time from the last frame's Present to this frame's drawing, the update in between, **not** the whole frame. What the hierarchy phase advances by where it is above 0.2. Also shown x 10000 among the render timings.
addresses.evidence: Three references: written at VA 0x656EA1 (`fld clock; fsub [0x1bea484]; fstp`), read at 0x6570E4 (the phase) and 0x657398 (x 10000.0, the double at 0x160A370). The clock is a CHighPerfWinClock in seconds (FINDINGS-tooltips.md, section 3). What would show it wrong: another writer.

addresses.name: g_RenderEndTime
addresses.comment: Float: the idler's frame clock read as the last thing CInGameIdler_Render does, after Present.
addresses.evidence: Two references: written at VA 0x658EA7 after `call 0xa73b80` (device slot 17, Present) and `call 0xa76e80`; read at 0x656E9A.

addresses.name: g_HierarchyHalfMapWidth
addresses.comment: Float, the map width (CMap +0x2A74) x 0.5, worked out by the first HierarchyLines_AddLine of the process (guard bit 0 of the dword at rva 0x17EB718) and kept: the seam test's half.
addresses.evidence: VA 0x882C26..0x882C5E: `test byte [0x1beb718],1; jne`; `or [0x1beb718],1`; the width converted, `mulsd [0x160A308]` (0.5), stored to 0x1BEB714. What would show it wrong: another writer of the guard.

struct_fields.name: records
struct_fields.comment: Begin of a vector of 8-byte records {CUnit* unit, CMapProvince* province} - every land unit aboard nothing that the last build walked, with the province it was in; +4 its end, +8 its capacity. HierarchyLines_IsCurrent compares the walk against it.
struct_fields.evidence: HierarchyLines_CountUnit appends {esi, [esi+0x130]} through 0x883B30 on the vector at [context+0] = the object; Rebuild's erase loop reads [ebx] and [ebx+4] with an 8-byte stride; IsCurrent's helper divides ([+4] - [+0]) by 8.

struct_fields.name: records_end
struct_fields.evidence: As +0: Rebuild's `mov [ebx+4],ecx` after the erase; the constructor zeroes it.

struct_fields.name: records_capacity
struct_fields.comment: End of the records vector's storage.
struct_fields.evidence: Zeroed with +0 and +4 by the constructor and HierarchyLines_Destruct; the third word of the std::vector, inferred from that shape.

struct_fields.name: commander
struct_fields.comment: The commander (+0x1E0) of the unit the mesh was built for; HierarchyLines_IsCurrent's first test.
struct_fields.evidence: Rebuild `mov ecx,[esi+0x1e0]; mov [ebx+0x10],ecx` at VA 0x8838D9; IsCurrent compares [unit+0x1E0] with it (the existing record's evidence).

struct_fields.name: has_lines
struct_fields.comment: Set by Rebuild when the mesh holds at least one line, cleared with no unit or no line; CInGameIdler::Update sets it to whether a land unit is selected; CInGameIdler_Render draws only while it is set.
struct_fields.evidence: Rebuild's stores at VA 0x8838A3, 0x88396E, 0x883A58; the render gate `cmp byte [edi+0x14],bl` at 0x6570DF.

struct_fields.name: phase
struct_fields.comment: hierarchy.fx's Time: 0.0 when made, never reset; each drawn frame CInGameIdler_Render adds g_RenderIdleSeconds where that is above 0.2 and 0.2 otherwise, and takes 100 off once it is above 100.
struct_fields.evidence: Constructor `movss [eax+0x18],xmm0` (0.0) at VA 0x64930D; the only writer besides is CInGameIdler_Render at 0x65712A/0x65713D; passed to HierarchyLines_Draw at 0x657148.

struct_fields.name: mesh
struct_fields.comment: The lines' mesh by value: 4 vertices of 24 bytes and 6 16-bit indices a line, managed pool, triangle list, g_HierarchyVertexDecl. HierarchyLines_Draw is handed its address.
struct_fields.evidence: Rebuild: `lea edi,[ebx+0x1c]` passed as the MeshBuffer to VertexBuffer_Create/IndexBuffer_Create; the render passes `add edi,0x1c` to HierarchyLines_Draw at 0x65714D, which reads +0x10 primitive_count and hands it to VertexBuffer_Draw.

struct_fields.name: hierarchy_lines
struct_fields.comment: The selected unit's hierarchy lines (a HierarchyLines, 0x40 bytes): the records it was built from at +0, the unit's commander at +0x10, a byte at +0x14 that there is something to draw, the picture's phase at +0x18, the mesh from +0x1C. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-hierarchy.md, sections 2 and 7.
struct_fields.evidence: Stored at VA 0x649334 from the 0x40-byte allocation the HierarchyLines declaration describes; read by CInGameIdler_Render at 0x657076/0x6570D9 and destroyed at 0x64981E..0x649829.
struct_fields.revises: type void* -> HierarchyLines*, now that the object has a struct; comment cites section 7 too.

struct_fields.name: frame_clock
struct_fields.comment: A second clock, made and started by CInGameIdler_Render on its first frame from g_random_object's slot 1 (a CHighPerfWinClock in seconds in a running game); read through its slot 5 for g_RenderIdleSeconds, g_RenderEndTime and the render timings. Distinct from +0x192C, the clock Enter makes.
struct_fields.evidence: VA 0x656E39..0x656E8C: `cmp [edi+0x1934],ebx; jne`, the factory at 0x174DA90, `mov [edi+0x1934],eax`, the clock's slot 1, then slot 5 (`call [edx+0x14]; fstp`). Every later `mov ecx,[edi+0x1934]` in the routine calls slot 5. What would show it wrong: a writer outside CInGameIdler_Render.
